title: The Last Choir
premise: Ivo Winterbourne, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Veth, keeps accounts for the Guild of Impossible Things, which survives by staying unrecorded in maps, memory, and law. When prayers to dead gods begin being answered across the country of Cael Sarn—officially dissolved forty years ago—the answers start naming guild members, and Ivo's own ledgers begin rewriting themselves. To escape, Ivo must find the Door of Unnaming hidden in the drowned capital, but opening it requires paying the god's debt with something irreplaceable: their memories of who they were before the oath. In the end, Ivo chooses to walk through the door nameless and free, leaving the ledgers behind as the only proof that they—and the country that made them—ever existed.
about_author: Cyrus Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing defunct institutions before turning to fiction. They write about people erased from official records, and live somewhere that does not appear on maps.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ivo audits the guild's winter accounts in the border town of Ashmoor, recording impossible trades: a stolen shadow, a borrowed year. A prayer whispered at a ruined shrine is answered aloud, and the answering voice uses Ivo's childhood name—one no living person knows. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the past knocking on a locked door.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Serah Quill convenes the members in the Unmapped Room, revealing that answered prayers are spreading and every one names someone the guild has sheltered. The ledgers Ivo keeps have begun annotating themselves with debts owed to Veth, the silent god. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dread of exposure; the safety of invisibility cracking.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ivo travels into old Cael Sarn to investigate a village where a dead god healed a dying child. The land remembers itself: roads reappear, bells ring in empty towers. Ivo meets Pell, a priest of Veth who never stopped praying. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: vertigo and reluctant wonder as the erased world resurfaces.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Pell shows Ivo a scripture naming 'the Winterbourne heir' as Veth's chosen debtor—Ivo's family once held the god's covenant. Ivo denies it, but fragments of suppressed memory surface: a mother's hymn, a burning chapel. POV: Ivo, with an interlude of Pell's testimony. Emotional beat: identity as inheritance one never asked for.

chapters.title: Collectors
chapters.summary: Agents of the Cartographic Office—bureaucrats who erase places—arrive hunting the resurgent Cael Sarn, and they capture Pell. Ivo escapes using guild tradecraft, learning the Office seeks the Door of Unnaming too, to close it forever. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; enemies on all sides.

chapters.title: The Drowned Capital
chapters.summary: Ivo returns to warn the guild, but Ashmoor is half-erased already, streets unwriting themselves. Serah reveals the Door lies beneath the flooded city of Vael Corin and that only a covenant-holder can open it. She asks Ivo to go alone. POV: Serah briefly, then Ivo. Emotional beat: betrayal-tinged duty; the guild's survival weighed against one life.

chapters.title: Hymns Under Water
chapters.summary: Ivo descends into drowned Vael Corin with diver-brother Caspian Ondu, navigating sunken cathedrals where the old gods sing. Veth finally speaks—not words but memory, flooding Ivo with the truth of their childhood oath, sworn by another's hand. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: grief and revelation; the self was never freely chosen.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: At the Door of Unnaming, Ivo learns its toll: the covenant-holder's entire memory of self. The Cartographic Office arrives; Pell, freed, dies holding the line so Ivo can choose. Veth offers to take the debt instead—but a god's payment would erase the whole country again. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; choosing what defines a person.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: Ivo refuses both tolls and instead writes themselves out of their own ledger—renouncing the oath, the guild, and the name—paying the door with authorship rather than memory. The Door opens onto elsewhere; the Office's erasure collapses harmlessly. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: liberation through surrender; identity reclaimed by letting it go.

chapters.title: The Last Choir
chapters.summary: On the far side, in a new country with no gods yet, a nameless traveler hears faint singing—Veth and the old gods, freed, becoming music rather than masters. The final ledger page records only: 'Account closed. All debts forgiven.' POV: Ivo, unnamed. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory carried without weight, inheritance transformed into song.
